evidence: app:/tmp/ws-980 (980b1a6, two actors): undo and startImport both have output ShopMessage (ui model Admin/(esm/__h9okOPQ...)/OperationType and startImport output target Admin/(esm/_-9UEcN4fEfGXQ5e6S2Rixw)/ClassType); Maven: mvn -o -f application/frontend-react/pom.xml -pl model -am compile then -pl webshop__admin generate-sources (EXIT 0); scan of webshop__admin/src: 2430 .ts/.tsx, 0 files with duplicate imported names; harness /tmp/r19b-1/harness/run-ws-980-Admin.txt: 0 duplicate pages. upstream: framework_issue: Reported: the duplicate-import build error happens on a model without a third actor, when an operation without input and another operation share an output type (ImportRunInfo undo and startImport both output ShopMessage). Not reproduced with the app's own Maven pipeline at 980b1a6: the two-actor generated admin sources contain no duplicate imported names, although the output type is shared. The duplicate needs a page that holds its own copy of a class while a later actor's copy of the same class is bound to one of its actions (see WR19-15). Expected: no duplicate type imports for any model. Evidence: Esm2UiZetaTransformation.java:847-907 (rebinding pass), UiPageHelper.java:176-181 (page import collection). Please send the failing model state if it still reproduces.

heading: Duplicate type imports with a third actor (known issue)
replaces: A third actor can break the generated frontend build: `./judo.sh build` stops at `pnpm run format` (biome) with `Declarations inside of a import declaration may not have duplicates` (for example `import type { CsvFile, CsvFile, ... }`) when an operation has an input and an output of the same type. The template emits one import per entry of `getApiImportsForPage`, built from a `HashSet<ClassType>` that deduplicates by object identity, so two `ClassType` objects for one class produce duplicate lines. It appears with any third actor (human or system, anonymous or not) and disappears when the third actor is removed. A two-actor build right after a model switch (for example after leaving a branch with the third actor) can show the same error from a stale, mixed model; run `./judo.sh generate` and `./judo.sh build -i` again before blaming the actor count. Workaround: keep the frontend to two actors and route the extra operation through an existing actor.
proposed: The generated admin frontend can fail in `pnpm run format` (biome) with `Declarations inside of a import declaration may not have duplicates` (for example `import type { <Entity>, <Entity>, ... }`). Cause: the ESM to UI transformation runs once per actor, in model file order. Each run rebinds the operation of every call-operation action in the shared UI model whose name matches a class and operation of the current actor (`Esm2UiZetaTransformation.java:847-907`). A page of an earlier actor that also holds its own copy of that class then imports the class twice: once from its own copy and once from the copy of the later actor. A shared output type alone does not trigger it, and a two-actor model with a shared output type generates without duplicates. Verified workaround: list the actor that exposes a class and operation also exposed by another actor first in the model file. The same model with that actor last fails with 12 duplicated admin pages (48 files); with it first, no file has a duplicate import.
evidence: mvn -o pipeline on worktree /tmp/ws-e7 (e7aa555, Guest last): admin generate-sources EXIT 0; scan: 48 files with duplicate imports in 12 admin pages (e.g. dialogs/ImportRunInfo/ImportRunInfo_Table/StartImport/Input/Form/customization.ts, duplicates ShopMessage / ShopMessageStored). Controlled: /tmp/ws-e7m (same commit, Guest moved first in model/webshop.model): 0 duplicate files; /tmp/ws-eea (eea170d, Guest first): 0. Harness /tmp/r19b-1/harness/H.java on the UI model: failing page OperationUnmappedInputPageDefinition AdminOrderInfo::...::exportOrders::Input::Form has two ClassType objects 'CsvFile': Admin/(esm/_slh9YN42EfGwOroSSM_LXg)/ClassType and Guest/(esm/_slh9YN42EfGwOroSSM_LXg)/ClassType. The Guest copy is reached through actionDefinition.operation of an Admin action: Guest/(esm/_vym9Yd42EfGwOroSSM_LXg)/OperationOutputParameterType via Esm2UiZetaTransformation.java:907 and UiPageHelper.java:181.
upstream: framework_issue: Reported: duplicate type imports in the generated admin frontend (import type { CsvFile, CsvFile, ... }) when a third actor is last in the model. Expected: each page imports a class once, whatever the actor order. Observed: worktree at e7aa555 with the actor last: 48 admin source files with duplicate imports; the same commit with that actor first: none. Cause: fixCallOperationActionDefinitions (Esm2UiZetaTransformation.java:835-907) runs for every actor in file order (:1720-1723) and collects the call-operation actions of all actors from the shared UI resource set (:847-858). It looks up the ClassType by the name prefix before '::' in the current actor's application only (findContainerClassType, :1182-1197), and then calls callOpDef.setOperation(clonedOp) (:907). The last actor therefore rebinds earlier actors' actions to its own copy of the operation. Expected: the lookup and the rebinding use the owning actor of the action, not the current actor. Evidence: admin action Admin/.../OperationType 'exportOrders' action operation -> Guest copy (126 cross-actor references in that model, 36 from Admin); UiPageHelper.java:181 adds the rebound output class next to the admin copy.

heading: Practice > Platform base
replaces: A third actor can break the generated frontend build when an operation has an input and an output of the same type (duplicate type imports; known issue, see [build process](../../agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md)). Workaround: keep the frontend to two actors and route the extra operation through an existing actor.
proposed: Actors are processed in model file order, and a later actor can rebind the operation of an earlier actor's action when both expose the same class and operation. A third actor can then cause duplicate type imports in the generated admin frontend (see [build process](../../agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md)). Place the actor that shares a class and operation with another actor first in the model file.
evidence: controlled: /tmp/ws-e7 (Guest last) 48 duplicate files; /tmp/ws-e7m (same commit, Guest moved to index 0 of the ActorType elements in model/webshop.model): 0 duplicate files; /tmp/ws-eea (eea170d, Guest first): 0. Code: runtime__judo-tatami-client/judo-tatami-esm2ui/src/main/java/hu/blackbelt/judo/tatami/esm2ui/zeta/Esm2UiZetaTransformation.java:1720-1723 (actor loop over getStreamOfEsmAccesspointActorType, file order), :847-858 (all call-operation actions collected), :888-907 (rebinding); UiPageHelper.java:181.
upstream: framework_issue: Reported: a third actor created last breaks the admin build; created first it passes; alphabetical name is irrelevant. Confirmed as file order, with the cause in the call-operation rebinding: for each actor the ESM to UI pass (Esm2UiZetaTransformation.java:1720-1723) lets fixCallOperationActionDefinitions (:835-907) rebind every earlier actor's call-operation action to the operation of the same name on its own ClassType copy (:888, :907), looked up by the name prefix in the current application (:1182-1197). Expected: an action keeps the operation of its owning actor, so the generated output is independent of actor order. Observed: 126 cross-actor operation references in the failing model (Admin and Customer actions pointing to Guest operations) versus 54 when Guest is first. Side observation, same transform: five Admin action ids are each used by two objects (ProductInfo category TabularReferenceField*Action); the transform log prints 'XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED' for them in every order.
